title: PAN format
text: A Permanent Account Number has 10 characters: 5 letters, 4 digits, then 1 letter (for example AABCA4821K). A value in any other format is not a valid PAN.

title: PAN holder type and name
text: The fourth character of a PAN shows the holder type; C means company. For a company bidder the name on the PAN card should match the legal name of the bidder.

title: GSTIN format
text: A GSTIN has 15 characters: a 2-digit state code, the 10-character PAN of the holder, a 1-character entity number, the letter Z, and a final check character.

title: PAN inside GSTIN
text: Characters 3 to 12 of a GSTIN are the PAN of the registered entity. The PAN on the PAN card must equal the PAN inside the GSTIN. A mismatch means the documents belong to different entities or one of them is wrong.

title: GST state code and address
text: The first two digits of a GSTIN are the state code (for example 29 is Karnataka). The state code should agree with the state in the registered principal place of business.

title: GST registration must be active
text: The GST registration must be active on the bid submission date. A cancelled or suspended registration, or a certificate whose validity date has passed, does not satisfy the requirement.

title: Udyam number format
text: An Udyam Registration Number looks like UDYAM-XX-00-0000000: the word UDYAM, a 2-letter state code, a 2-digit district code and a 7-digit serial number.

title: MSME category
text: Udyam registration classifies an enterprise as Micro, Small or Medium based on investment and turnover limits notified by the Ministry of MSME. The limits change over time and should be checked at the source.

title: MSE preference and relaxations
text: Tenders may give Micro and Small Enterprises benefits such as relaxed experience or turnover conditions and exemption from earnest money. Whether a benefit applies depends on the tender's own conditions, so the officer should confirm it.
source: Public Procurement Policy for MSEs Order 2012 and GFR 2017 (summary)

title: OEM authorization letter contents
text: When a tender asks for manufacturer authorization, the letter should come from the OEM and name the authorized bidder, the products covered, and a validity period. A letter that names a different bidder or different products does not satisfy the requirement.

title: OEM letter validity
text: The OEM authorization must still be valid on the bid submission date and should cover the bid validity and delivery period. An expired letter, or one that expires before the bid validity ends, should be flagged for officer review.

title: Local supplier classes
text: Under the Make in India procurement order, a Class-I local supplier has local content of 50 percent or more, a Class-II local supplier has 20 percent or more but less than 50 percent, and a supplier below 20 percent is non-local.
source: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017

title: Tender threshold for local content
text: If a tender sets a minimum local content (for example 50 percent), a bidder who declares a lower percentage does not meet the requirement. The comparison is a plain numeric check: the declared value must be at least the tender minimum.
source: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017 and tender conditions

title: Proof of local content
text: Local content is normally supported by a self-declaration; for larger procurements a certificate from a statutory auditor or cost auditor may be required. If the declared value is below the minimum, the officer can request clarification or a supporting certificate.
source: Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order 2017 (summary)

title: Debarred or blacklisted bidders
text: A bidder that is debarred or blacklisted by the government is not eligible to bid during the debarment period. The check compares bidder identifiers such as GSTIN or PAN against a debarment list.

title: Debarment data in this prototype
text: This prototype checks a simulated debarment list stored in a local file, not a live government register. Results must be labelled Simulated, and a real deployment would need an authorized connection to the official source.

title: Name mismatch across documents
text: Company name mismatch: the legal name of the bidder should be the same on the PAN card, GST certificate, Udyam certificate and OEM letter. A different company name on any document should be flagged for review. Small formatting differences such as Pvt Ltd versus Private Limited are acceptable.

title: Address mismatch across documents
text: Address mismatch: the registered address on the GST certificate and the Udyam certificate should refer to the same place. A clear difference in street, city, state or pincode should be flagged for the officer.

title: Low confidence extraction
text: When a field was read with low confidence or could not be found in the document text, the check result should be Review, not Pass or Fail, so that the officer verifies the original document.

title: Human decision
text: The system only recommends. The Procurement Officer makes the final decision: qualify, disqualify, or request clarification. The system must never disqualify a bidder on its own.
